column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/devshell-cargo-test-selftest.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHAT THIS WORKFLOW IS. The in-repo caller of the fleet reusable
# nix-devshell-cargo-test.yml, added because a shared reusable with no caller
# inside substrate cannot go red before its blast radius does — on 2026-07-27 a
# new `cargo-test` leg's first execution anywhere was in somebody else's CI. It
# runs BOTH directions of that gate: `green` calls the real reusable against a
# supported devShell, `green_evidence` proves the tests genuinely executed
# (cargo exits 0 on a suite that ran zero tests), `red` drives the preflight at
# a devShell that does not exist and asserts it refuses, and `verdict` fails the
# run unless all three actually succeeded.
# THIS WORKFLOW HAS NO SELECTION AXIS. Measured, not assumed: three of its four
# jobs carry no `if:` at all, and the fourth carries `if: always()`. There are
# no workflow inputs (`workflow_dispatch` declares none), no repo-type dispatch,
# no toggle, and no `github.*` read in any condition. So the single row below is
# not a sample of the input space — it IS the input space, and it is the
# denominator every future finding is measured against.
# WHAT THE ONE ROW THEREFORE PINS. That all four jobs select on every trigger.
# Any `if:` added to any job from here on makes this row red in one of two ways:
# the condition reads a context path this row does not declare (EVAL error), or
# it changes the selected set (NOT-RUN / RAN). That is the entire point, and the
# edit it is aimed at is a specific and tempting one — this workflow's own
# header notes it "burns two nix installs, so it is not on every push", and the
# obvious next economy is gating `red` or `green_evidence` behind
# `github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`. That edit leaves the on-push and
# on-PR runs proving ONE direction while staying green, which is precisely the
# both-directions guarantee this selftest exists to hold. This row is what says
# so.
# WHY ONLY always() IS DECLARED. This linter errors on a context path a
# condition READS and the case does not declare; a declared path nothing reads
# is inert. So the shortest honest context is the strongest tripwire — adding a
# speculative `github.event_name=push` key here would buy nothing and would
# pre-absorb exactly the failure described above.
# WHY always() IS TRUE. GitHub's always() is unconditionally true; no input
# makes it false. A row setting always()=false would model a state the platform
# cannot produce, and an impossible state asserted green is the failure mode
# this tool exists to prevent.
# ── WHAT THIS TABLE CANNOT SEE, so its green is not read as broader ─────────
# 1. DROPPING `if: always()` FROM `verdict` IS NOT CAUGHT, and this is the
#    honest limit worth knowing before trusting the row. verdict needs
#    [green, green_evidence, red], none of which has an `if:`, so all three
#    always select, needs-propagation never bites, and verdict selects with or
#    without always(). The always() here is load-bearing for the FAILED-
#    dependency half of its job — the half that makes a broken direction fail
#    the run instead of vanishing — and this linter has no failure state: a job
#    is selected or it is not, and there is no way to say "red ran and exited
#    1". Asserting that half would require faking always()=false, which is a
#    lie about the platform, so it is left unasserted rather than counterfeited.
# 2. `needs.green.result` / `.green_evidence.result` / `.red.result` are read
#    only inside verdict's `run:` block, never in an `if:`. Step bodies are
#    below this linter's resolution entirely. "verdict ran" below means the JOB
#    selected — never that its three `[ … ] || exit 1` assertions passed.
# 3. `green` is `uses:` a reusable. This row asserts the CALL is made and
#    nothing about what happens inside nix-devshell-cargo-test.yml, which has no
#    .cases.tsv of its own today (one unconditional job, `cargo-test`).
# 4. The push/pull_request `paths:` filters decide whether the workflow is
#    TRIGGERED at all. Trigger filtering is not job selection; no row here can
#    say "this workflow did not start".
# 5. NO JOB HERE PUBLISHES, DEPLOYS OR PUSHES — nothing is bumped, tagged,
#    released or written outside the runner; `red`'s only side effect is a
#    `nix eval` and verdict's is an `echo`. So the mandatory do-it /
#    don't-do-it publish rows of the sweep have no counterpart here. That
#    absence is itself a claim this header pins, so the next reader does not go
#    hunting for a row that should not exist.
# THE ONLY REACHABLE SHAPE. Both directions plus the evidence job plus the
# verdict, on every one of the three triggers. If this row ever needs a sibling,
# a condition was added to this workflow and the sibling is the proof it was
# added deliberately.
every-trigger-runs-both-directions
